summary_html: Agency or actor engages in **discriminatory or retaliatory action**, violating civil-rights or placement-equality provisions. Federal statutes prohibit race, religion, sex, or disability bias in placements or investigations.
authority_html:
- **Multiethnic Placement Act (MEPA) & Interethnic Adoption Provisions (IEP)** — prohibits race/ethnicity discrimination in placements  
- **Civil Rights Act (42 U.S.C. § 2000d)** — Title VI discrimination prohibitions in federally funded programs

key_cases.case_name: Arkansas Department of Human Services v. Cole
key_cases.holding: The court struck down Initiated Act 1, which barred cohabiting unmarried adults from adopting or fostering, holding that conditioning the privilege of fostering or adopting on surrendering the state constitutional right to private consensual conduct is unconstitutional.
key_cases.relevance: With Howard, it is the controlling Arkansas authority invalidating class-wide exclusion from foster and adoptive placement.
key_cases.quote: We affirm the circuit court's ruling that Act 1 is unconstitutional as a violation of fundamental privacy rights under the Arkansas Constitution.

key_cases.case_name: Arkansas Department of Human Services v. Howard
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed the invalidation of the Child Welfare Agency Review Board regulation barring any household with a homosexual adult from fostering, holding the rule had no rational relationship to child welfare and was an unauthorized exercise of legislative power over morality.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading Arkansas case striking a discriminatory placement rule, and it shows discriminatory intent being proved from the decisionmakers' own testimony.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court did not err in finding that there was no rational relationship between the regulation's blanket exclusion and the health, safety, and welfare of the foster children

key_cases.holding: The court reversed and ordered custody awarded to the appellant, holding the circuit court clearly erred by applying only a general best-interest test and failing to find good cause before departing from the ICWA placement preferences and the tribe's recommendation.
key_cases.relevance: Disregarding tribal placement preferences is the placement-equality failure ICWA was enacted to prevent.
key_cases.quote: The circuit court disregarded the ICWA preferences, specifically the recommendation of the Nation, and relied solely on the general "best interest" standard.

key_cases.case_name: Elkins v. Arkansas Department of Human Services
key_cases.holding: The court reversed the permanency-planning order and every order entered after it, holding that changing the goal to adoption alone, while an approvable relative placement was pending, contravened the ICWA placement preferences and applied the wrong burden of proof.
key_cases.relevance: Bonding with a non-ICWA-compliant foster placement cannot be used to deviate from the tribal placement preferences.
key_cases.quote: the circuit court clearly erred by changing the case's goal to solely adoption following termination in contravention of the preferences mandated by the ICWA
